articleTitle: Pasture Terrain Research via Drone
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The study of the terrain of the pastures leads to significant benefits for the conditions of livestock rearing. The main indicator of the cultivation method is the slope of the pasture terrain. The present study presents data on the slope of a selected pasture in the Republic of Bulgaria. The pasture is mountainous, located in the Rhodope Mountains. The results show high values of the studied indicator, which does not affect the overall free breeding of livestock in this region. The conducted research includes a comparison of the slope in three consecutive years from 2021 to 2023. The goal is to evaluate the possible changes that occur in upland grasslands as a result of natural processes.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Three-Phase Grid-Connected Solid-Oxide Fuel Cell Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This paper presents a method for modeling and simulating three-phase grid-connected solid-oxide fuel cell systems in the Matlab/Simulink environment. The approach is utilized to analyze the interaction between solid-oxide fuel cells and the electrical power system, focusing on understanding the dynamics of the electrochemical reaction and its impact on the performance of grid-connected fuel cell systems. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately modeling and operating three-phase grid-connected solid-oxide fuel cell systems.

Author Keywords: modeling, simulation, solid-oxide fuel cell, grid-connected

articleTitle: Development of an IoT-Based System for Recovery of Potential-Induced Degradation in PV Strings
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Different types of degradations of photovoltaic modules are known to significantly reduce their energy production. In this study is presented an IoT-based system for automatic regeneration of potential-induced degradation (PID), which is based on the string reconfiguration approach. A general architecture of the system is presented as well as an operation algorithm of the IoT modules, describing their behavior. Next, hardware components were selected for implementation of the system and a circuit schematic was created. The developed IoT-based system could be used for automatic compensation of PID in photovoltaic installations. Such approach could lead to significant improvement of the revenue during their long-term exploitation.

articleTitle: Variant Study of the Electrical Energy Supply to an Autonomous Consumer by Means of Wind Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The need to introduce into operation renewable energy sources, which successfully compete with the conventional energy producing resources, is considered in this paper. The advantages and disadvantages of the renewable energy sources are described. The paper presents a conducted variant study of the wind potential at two locations and analyzes the obtained results for the optimal power supply to an autonomous load with a known load profile, accomplished by means of wind power plants. The criteria for choosing the optimal option are: maximum energy yield of the wind power plants and discounted costs.

articleTitle: Possibility for extension of the production tolerance of a cylindrical gauge by relating it to risks Type I and Type II when controlling the functional surfaces of electrical motors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: It is known that gauges are scaleless alternative control tools that can control several parameters at the| same time, both fast and efficiently. Very often such are the parameters of surfaces of electrical motors. Expectedly, their usage requires a large number of parts having parameters with identical tolerance interval. From a technological point of view, the use of gauges for controlling dimensions having IT6 or having smaller tolerances is inefficient because the production of such gauges is extremely hard and expensive (they are rarely used in practice). The production tolerance for the working surfaces of gauges ranges from IT6 to IT10 for features of size up to 50 mm is about $4 \mu \mathrm{m}$, which is a complicated task even for modern cutting machine tools. The question about increasing this tolerance by several micrometers (e.g., 1-2 $\mu \mathrm{m}$) remains open or there is a requirement for admitting a specific value for the Type I ($\alpha$) error, i.e., there is a customer requirement for A Q L. This condition is normally related to the producer’s risk (the so called $\alpha$ error or a conforming part to be considered as a non-conforming one) but, of course, it is also directly related to the customer’s risk ($\beta$ error-a non-conforming part is considered as a conforming one).

Author Keywords: scaleless alternative control tools for electrical motors

articleTitle: The Process Approach in Artificial Intelligence Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Management systems help organizations achieve their strategic direction, and enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of their processes. The ISO management system standards are based on a pivotal principle - the process approach. The first edition of ISO 42001 - the standard for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Management Systems (MS) was published in December 2023. This is a good opportunity for organizations to keep up to date with the modern context and integrate AI into their MS. This paper presents a model that helps to establish the input clauses and output clauses of individual ISO 42001 processes, better understand the interactions between the processes, and create an overall view and representation of the AI MS based on these processes.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic System for Pulse Charging of Battery Power Supply of Sensor Devices in Greenhouses
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: For remote measurement of meteorological quantities in greenhouses and in livestock buildings, the use of energy-independent sensors is appropriate. To provide local supply voltage, low-output photovoltaic panels and rechargeable batteries can be used. In this article, a new method of converting the DC energy of the solar panel into AC and then again into DC is studied, with the possibility of dosing the amount of electric charge needed to charge the battery. The conversion of DC energy from the photovoltaic panel to an AC one is carried out by a sequentially switched on single-polar rectangular pulse generator, a bandpass filter and a parallel resonant circuit. The parallel resonant circuit consumes a minimum amount of energy at resonance, but provides a current of much greater value for generating charging pulses for the battery. The basic equations describing the processes of electrical energy conversion are derived. The results of the experimental study of the bandpass filter and the resonance circuit as well as the parameters of the current pulses for charging the accumulator are presented. The possibility of adjusting the amplitude value of charge pulses was investigated.

Author Keywords: Variable duty cycle pulse charge system

articleTitle: Advanced management technologies for intelligent cattle breeding systems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of applying advanced technologies as a tool to manage biological units of a specific population of cattle reared on well-defined pasture areas with the aim of efficient and intelligent livestock management.

articleTitle: Development of a methodological approach for the analysis of urban metabolism
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: An increase in the population of cities and the tendency to form urban agglomerations inevitably lead to more complex transport, energy and utility infrastructure. Which in turn increases the requirements for managing and streamlining the flow of energy resources and waste generated in urban areas. The term ‘‘urban metabolism” appears in the scientific and technical literature in the mid-60s. At the same time, urban metabolism is often considered in the context of political, historical or social sciences, leaving out of focus the energy, technological and environmental aspects of the functioning of the metropolis.

articleTitle: Extending the life of batteries through rational exploitation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The development of the car market in the direction of electric traction, but also in general, the increasing use of electricity storage in batteries, has generated an approach regarding the duration of use of batteries. In order to reduce costs, we are trying to find solutions to increase the duration of their use. Regardless of the constructive type of batteries, there is a limit to the number of chargingdischarging them. For a period of time, the idea of this article is to reduce the number of charge-discharges, which can be achieved by using the battery’s charge and discharge limits to the maximum. An algorithm is developed through which a hysteresis charging-discharging characteristic is exploited. The designed and analyzed device monitors the charging status of the battery and starts and ends the charging process, only under certain conditions. The device was developed with the idea of very easy introduction into already existing electrical equipment, placing itself between the battery and the charging source.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Potential of Savonius Wind Turbines for Low-Wind Energy Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The primary objective of this paper was to design a small-scale Savonius wind turbine well suited for providing autonomous power to an embedded system. We analyzed the potential of energy production using a vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT), which is a renewable energy source suitable for use in areas with low wind energy potential. Using SolidWorks software, we did a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation in order to examine the behavior of six different types of Savonius turbines, presenting different numbers of blades and different helical blade angles. Finally, we constructed a Savonius turbine measuring 25 cm in diameter and 50 cm in height, featuring helical blades with a twist angle of 360-degree, capable of generating power at a minimum blade speed of 6 rad/s.

articleTitle: Constructive Parametric Modeling Of The Fuel Supply Law For Building A Synergetic System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: abstract-The specifics of fueling in the field of physic-chemical processes and dynamics still have unexplained transient processes and subprocesses, which should generate additional multiple indicators for evaluation and analysis of the elements of a system. As part of a synergistic system, the developed models based on the examined stages of fuel supply bring greater clarity to the dynamics, despite the simplified calculation methods used to specify the model. The necessary simplification and the use of known dependencies is caused by the insufficiently high potential capabilities of modern electronics for real-time database processing on multi-channel input. The application of these models gives a complete view of a synergistic system for management and diagnostic purposes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the electrical characteristics of Hall elements made of Germanium and Gallium Arsenide
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Hall elements are among the most widely used magnetic sensing components in electronics, finding applications in various fields depending on the material they are made of - such as silicon, gallium arsenide, germanium, and others. To choose the optimal sensor for a specific application, it is essential to understand the parameters of different materials. Properly selecting the sensor not only facilitates the design of various systems but also significantly enhances the application’s efficiency by providing more accurate and reliable results. This selection process is key to the successful implementation of magnetic sensing devices and systems in any industry. The automated DX50 system, which is used, significantly streamlines engineers’ work by providing values for various parameters such as Hall coefficient and voltage, carrier mobility, resistivity, and others. Calculations are based on the Van der Pauw method, ensuring high data accuracy. This measurement system greatly reduces the time required for measurements and decreases the likelihood of error in measurement and calculation, providing more reliable and accurate results.

articleTitle: Robot to collect cattle droppings from pastures - concept
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The present work addresses the issue of conceptual development of a mobile robot for cow excreta collection in pasture rearing. The issue is very topical, since the role of organic animal husbandry is increasingly being addressed in order to obtain products with high quality indicators, and on the other hand the area of pasture is decreasing. The transition from standard livestock farming to intelligent livestock farming is very much on the agenda, which is why various concepts for rotational grazing are being developed. In this work, the problem is analyzed and a conceptual model of a robot is proposed by defining and classifying the systems it should possess.

articleTitle: Research of Electromagnetic Field Distribution When UHF-Drying Wool in the Device
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The distribution of the electromagnetic field in a wool drying device, calculating the antenna device and the dependence of the duration of drying wool at a volumetric density of ultra-high frequency (UHF) power of $0,01 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$, the duration of drying wool when changing the volumetric density of UHF power, the duration of heating wool for the volumetric density of UHF energy $0,01 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$, duration of wool drying during cyclic heating for a volumetric UHF energy density of $0,01 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$, spectral analysis of wool are considered in the article.

articleTitle: Developing and Evaluating IoT- based Digital Farming and Environmental Security Course: Al Istiqlal University Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The internet of things (IoT) is an emerging paradigm of applications of innovative technologies in the current educational era. Using IoT technology tools assists teachers develop the experience available to students more than the traditional curriculum. The purpose of this study was to describe the designed course on digital farming and environmental security as well as the students’ assessment of such curricula. A questionnaire was designed and its validity was tested in order to attain these objectives. All 35 students enrolled in Al Istiqlal University’ s (PASS) GIS department were included in the study sample. Team from PASS developing digital farming and environmental security course using the innovative IoT technology. Training adopted the TPACK instructional design model, which is characterized by a complicated interaction between technological, pedagogical, and content knowledge. The trained team produced the Terms of Reference (ToR) by defined all the educational aspects of the developed new course such as goal, objectives and intended learning outcomes. Based on the produced ToR, the trained team developed digital farming and environmental security course curricula and syllabus. AgriLive monitoring system were installed in the date palm farms to provide an applied learning environment that enhances the knowledge contained in the curriculum. The results of this research indicated that all of the study tool’ s questions were accepted by the students, supporting the development of the course in accordance with the PASS model. With an average of (3.32), the overall level of students’ assessment of the curriculum and materials was high. The overall means for assessing students’ understanding of the designed course and their assessment of its contents and curriculum came out on high level with means of (3.33) and (3.31), respectively. This study recommend this developed course as a new model to be adopted from the universities in Palestine.

articleTitle: Energy Management To Provide Multiple Services From Battery To Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Batteries may provide ancillary services to the power network and thus can be used as a energy storage tool. In this paper, we examine the income of the battery owner, the amount of energy drawn from the battery, and the amount of change in the state of the charge (SOC) by considering different cases. For this aim, our study uses real data of frequency, voltage, load, energy market prices and house power production and consumption profiles. From the simulation results obtained we observe that the profit that battery owners can make as a result of using these services is of great importance for the energy market of the future and the battery to grid system is crucial solution for minimizing problems caused by abnormal frequency, voltage, load, etc. in the network.

articleTitle: Weather Monitoring System Using IoT-based DIY Automatic Weather Station
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of a weather monitoring system representing the data collected by a do-it-yourself (DIY), Internet of Things (IoT)-based automatic weather station. The system displays the gathered data through three distinct platforms: a dedicated website, an Android application and the ThingSpeak cloud platform. The automatic weather station stores the weather parameter data in its own database. A developed script extracts the data from the database and sends it to the website and ThingSpeak platform where it is represented appropriately. The Android app presents the website interface in the form of a mobile application. The system has been implemented successfully and reliably performs weather monitoring, providing the user with personal choice, accessibility and mobility. It is easy to implement and uses free and open-source software.

articleTitle: Dependency for Determination and Distribution of Tangential Tensions of Flows in Smooth Pipes at Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The movement of fluids between the different layers within the flow, as well as the passing flow over solid surfaces, generates resistance forces - tensions, resulting from the viscosity of the fluid and the pulsational alteration of instantaneous velocities. The determination of these tensions is necessary and important for theory and practice of irrigation processes to achieve greater precision in agricultural activities. Increasing the energy efficiency of irrigation water transportation and distribution processes will be also achieved. For this purpose, many experimental, analytical and field studies have been carried out on turbulent tensions only for some specific condition or for real situation of a given facility, which actually shows the necessity of a realistic theoretical and analytical dependence on this subject. In the present work, a theoretical dependence is established for the distribution and values of turbulent tensions in flows in hydraulically smooth pipes, applicable to various velocity distribution diagrams under a power-graded law distribution, as well as for velocity distribution according to a logarithmic law function. The obtained relation is confirmed by experimental results given in the literature.

articleTitle: Laboratory Verification of Simulation Studies of Bipolar Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: A precise knowledge of the output parameters of a semiconductor element (transistor) is particularly important in its optimal choice for a specific application. In the last decade, the classical characterization using a laboratory setup has received an effective alternative with dedicated compact measuring instruments. The paper presents a simulated study of a powerful bipolar transistor using a tester. Its results are compared and verified by the classic laboratory method with a bench.

articleTitle: Modeling of the operation of DC motor with series excitation in Matlab environment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: In this article a virtual model in Matlab program environment is made, which serves for the study of a DC motor with series excitation. The stages of building the model and the way of acquiring data to construct the performance characteristics of the engine are presented. The simulations are done in a way that the study correlates to the real experiments. This gives the opportunity to be compared the results obtained from the simulations and the ones obtained in the laboratory environment. The obtained results are analyzed. The working capacity of the model is proven.

articleTitle: Intelligent systems and technologies in the field of hotel services
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The purpose of the article is to analyze the effectiveness of implementation and management in the hotel sector using artificial intelligence and automated management. The article used as the main tool the analysis of statistical data from open sources, as well as surveys of respondents aged 18 to 50. The article discusses the capabilities of artificial intelligence, which can improve the efficiency of doing business, by introducing chat bots, maintaining a hotel analyst, creating automatic responses, automatically closing sales channels, analyzing competitors, assessing quality control, proposals for improving business management, automatically notifying guests about departure and collection of subsequent data into a single database. Increasing sales efficiency and maintaining the marketing component of the business, saving employee time on basic operational processes. In addition to the obvious advantages, the use of artificial intelligence also carries certain risks and disadvantages. Effective management of AI requires a team to monitor its actions and control system errors that accumulate as a result of its work. There may be a leak of user data, as well as the use of user data by artificial intelligence in a negative way for them. Artificial intelligence is not able to replace simple human communication; at the moment, an increasing number of companies are using various chatbots and there is a certain human fatigue from the constant presence of automated responses to user requests. The security architecture on which artificial intelligence is built still needs to be refined because does not have significant protection, because most developments are start-ups without proper funding and proper verification by the government apparatus.

articleTitle: Theoretical prerequisites for improving the efficiency of tractor operation in agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Agricultural production is characterize by the seasonality of mechanized work in the cultivation of crops. In addition, the amount of wear on aggregates and equipment systems is determined, on the one hand, by natural and climatic conditions (the presence of slopes and obstacles; humidity, dustiness and air temperature) and, on the other, by the nomenclature of operations performed in the planned period, organizational, production and technical conditions in a particular farm. It should also be note that tractor units and systems are interconnect with each other and interdependent on each other, i.e. the amount of wear of some parts affects the wear of others. Based on the above, in our opinion, one of the promising ways to improve the efficiency of tractors is to develop measures to optimize the resource consumption of tractor units and systems, taking into account the variety of changing factors of tractor operation in the cultivation of crops. This requires a comprehensive parameter that takes into account not only the wear of the part, but also the degree of its impact on the wear of the unit as a whole and gives us the opportunity to develop measures to optimize it. Such an indicator is the level of resource consumption of the unit, the system and tractors as a whole. With known patterns of changes in the level of resource consumption for various types of agricultural operations, it becomes possible to plan the range of work for each tractor for the planned period, taking into account the optimal resource consumption of their units and systems. This article examines the theoretical prerequisites for justifying the level of resource consumption and reveals its potential for solving the problem of increasing the efficiency of tractor operation in the agro-industrial complex.

articleTitle: Application of fuzzy logic to short-term planning of electric loads
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The paper presents the difference between planning and forecasting in electrical power distribution networks. Fuzzy logic implementation in predicting electric loads in distribution networks for a day-long period is described. The main requirements toward forecasting of electric loads are taken into account and the following influencing factors are considered: the time (the hour t of the 24-hour load schedule, for which the forecast value is sought), the realized value of the load from the same hour of the previous day (for time t-24), and the climatic conditions (temperature). The structural scheme of the methodology of load predicting by applying fuzzy logic has been presented.The following fuzzy logic rules are applied: fuzzifying the input data and presenting them as membership functions; compiling the fuzzy rules base, making a conclusion about the estimated value of the load and applying defuzzification. The fuzzy output is converted into an exact number, corresponding to the estimated value of the load. The error in the day-ahead short-term forecasting of the electric load in a specific electrical distribution network (EDN) when applying fuzzy logic is within +2,4% to -1,7%. Conclusions are drawn from the application of fuzzy logic in forecasting the electric loads in an EDN for a day ahead.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of the Temperature Field of a Flexible PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The reliability of electronic modules is strongly dependent on their temperature regime. This study presents results about the influence of different parameters of flexible polyimid PCBs and the environment on the temperature field of the device. It is conducted with a specially developed software tool, which implements a previously developed model. The factors that are being analyzed are the dissipated heat by the SMD component, the percentage of the copper layer area from the total area of the PCB, the thickness of the copper layer, the thickness of the PCB, and the air velocity. The obtained results allow us to conclude the two of the parameters have the highest impact on the reduction of the PCB temperature - the copper layer percentage area from the total area of the PCB, and the thickness of the copper layer. To obtain optimal results in terms of thermal regime as well as investment, it is recommended to combine the different approaches together.

articleTitle: Use of Unmanned Aircraft for Assessment of Maize Vegetation in Southern Dobruja
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Remote monitoring used for assessment of crops development serves the needs of precision agriculture in the attempt of improving the quality of agricultural products. The aim of this work is to evaluate the effectiveness of eight plant indices identifying the maize vegetation at southern Dobrudja in 2021. The source of empirical data for this survey are the multispectral images obtained from a digital NIR camera mounted on a remotely piloted drone. Two distinct fields with maize crops were inspected at the Dobruja district, Bulgaria within the period of intensive growth. Eight vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI2, SAVI, NDWI, RDVI, CVI, MGVRI, MPRI) are estimated in the experiment and seven of them led to a general trend of the index change. The applied method of data collection and post-processing approach give satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Monitoring the homogeneity of temperature fields in thermal chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Temperature being a non-electrical quality requires additional sensors and circuitry to measure, monitor and control. It is present in our daily life everywhere, whether we want a cozy feel in out apartment or we want to make sure that the latest ECU developed for the latest car model will work in Norway as well as in India. Thermal chambers allow us to test electronics prior to their release on the market to make sure that they meet the technical specifications we want. In a niche environment, thermal chambers are used to solder the SMD components on the PCBs, being part of reflow ovens. For desktop size reflow ovens, the temperature behavior is particularly important due to the standards we need to follow in order to ensure a repetitive and reproducible reflow profile. For this purpose, the monitor solution designed, build and tested is presented in this article.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Triticale Grain Yield After Pre-Sowing Electromagnetic Seed Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: A three-factor field experiments were conducted during the period 2017-2019. In the study, the seeds were presowing treated with an electromagnetic field, and during their growth, mineral and organic fertilizers were applied. The electromagnetic field parameters were determined using preliminary laboratory tests. Based on the obtained results, the different influence of electromagnetic treatment and fertilization on the yield of the two triticale varieties (“Boomerang” and “Colorit”) is confirmed. The complex influence of factors on the variety “Boomerang” was established. For this variety, an $8.6 \%$ yield increase was obtained when electromagnetic seed treatment was applied. The application of fertilizers increased the yield by $3.6 \%$ and $20.8 \%$.

articleTitle: Designing and Examining Reactive (LC) Filters Using Computerized Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This paper presents the processes of designing and examining low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, and band-stop filters of type “K” and type “m” (series-derivative and parallel-derivative) using different computerized tools. This is done based on data about the nominal characteristic impedance, cutoff (mean) frequency, and coefficient m (for derivative filters only). The designing process is implemented using MATLAB, and the examination process of the designed filters after the selection of standard values of the capacitances of the capacitors in the synthesized circuits is performed using MicroCAP. The results will be used in the learning process of the courses “Communication Circuits”, “Signals and Systems”, and “Power Supply” studied by the students of the specialties “Internet and Mobile Communications”, “Computer Systems and Technologies” and “Electronics” of the “Bachelor” degree.

articleTitle: An IoT-based System for Monitoring and Control of Irrigation Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The application of information and communication technologies in modern agriculture is the key for implementing precision agriculture. This study presents the development of some of the components of a complex IoT-based irrigation system, communicating over LoRaWAN. An IoT electronic module is developed, which is used to collect information about the soil parameters and send it over to a remote server. The module is powered by a small PV panel and a battery. A prototype of the IoT device is implemented and its operation algorithm is presented with a flow chart. The study also presents the design of a database, which is able to hold all the necessary information about the operation of the irrigation system.

articleTitle: Determination of Photocell Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The present article presents research on the experimental determination of photodiode parameters. The main characteristics of semiconductor elements used in microelectronics are presented. An algorithm for determining efficiency is discussed, and several dependencies between the incident light flux per unit area and the generated energy are derived. A virtual instrument created based on the LabVIEW software platform and the DAC data acquisition module EMANT 300 is presented. Virtual instruments are multifunctional and flexible platforms that can be used both in the learning process and for scientific research. They combine precise hardware with the flexibility of a standard personal computer, offering its power, standard applications (the ability to visualize and process collected data), and communication capabilities. The presented model can be conveniently used in the educational process for various disciplines, catering to students from different specialties such as electronics, automation, and others.

articleTitle: The Study the Compost Mass Moisture and the Degree of Straw Crushing Effect on Compost Temperature in a Multifactorial Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The composting of crop and livestock waste multifactorial experiment was conducted in order to determine the main controlled factors impact such as humidity and straw crushing degree on the composting process. The experiment allows to measure the values of controlled factors in the composting process, at which the maximum compost temperature was reached. The influence degree of two main controlled factors - the humidity content of the material $X_{1}(W)$ and the straw length $X_{3}$ (n) on the composting was determined, with an optimal of carbon/nitrogen ratio $X_{2}(C: N)-40.1$. The composting process that was influenced by controlled factor, was studied and the reliability coefficient of approximation $R^{2}$ for each controlled factor was determined.

articleTitle: A Synergetic Approach for the Analysis of Volume Mixture Formation in Modern Marine Diesel Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The synergistic approach to diagnostics and management is the development of the latest generation of management and diagnostics systems. The basis of this approach is the common use of databases from the construction and operation tasks. The constructive task exists on the basis of real mass-dimensional characteristics and parameters, and the operational one needs a larger experimental base to fulfill the set goal. These systems can also generate expert advice and work as a twin system to the imaged object.

articleTitle: Modeling of the processes of using agricultural machinery products for automation of personal subsidiary farms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The purpose of the article is to develop an imitation innodiversification model and to test mathematical software that would cover a wide range of different types of activities of personal subsidiary farms and take into account the features of their automation based on modern agricultural engineering products. The article used as the main tool a simulation modeling technique based on the theory of Petri nets, which involves the formation of a structure of operations in the automation of economic activities of personal subsidiary farms, which allows describing the structure or process of any type of activity in a format that determines which transitions are performed at which position and in what sequence. The basis of the innodiversification approach to simulation modeling is the formation of such a structure of operations that could clearly simulate the order of execution of technological processes of organizations of personal subsidiary farms closest to real situations. It is proved that the proposed technique makes it possible to transform the resulting graphical structure into mathematical models in the form of tuples and matrices. As an example, the practical implementation of the proposed algorithm in the Simulator application package is given. It has been established that simulation model design using innodiversification Petri nets is the optimal, if not the only possible way to improve the structure of production systems and technological processes of organizations automating personal subsidiary farms, as well as their associations, and the management of these structures.

articleTitle: Potential Use of the Vibroacoustic Analysis of an Engine in the Analysis of Exhaust Gases Composition
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The paper presents the vibration of an engine powered by various fuels in the emission function. There is extensive literature on emissivity research results, yet no analysis on the results of the degree to which vibroacoustic vibration generated by the engine may generate diagnostic information on exhaust emission composition has been discussed so far. As it was shown, the vibroacoustic characteristics analysis differs for various fuels mixtures, new additional harmonics appear and the values of dominant harmonics change. Proving the similarity between vibration characteristics, based on the fast Fourier transform filter, and exhaust emission composition may pave an entirely new diagnostic path.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of an Electric Transport High-Power Three-Phase Full-Wave Uncontrolled Rectifier in the MATLAB/Simulink Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: A three-phase full-wave high-power uncontrolled rectifier of a power substation of electric trolleybus transport system has been modelled and simulated in the programming environment of MATLAB/Simulink. The obtained simulation results are analysed and they confirmed the mathematical descriptions of the electrical processes and semiconductor device principles. The shapes of the currents and voltages are analysed and solution guidelines are given to reduce the non-sinusoidal distortions of the currents. The developed model can find application in the modelling and studying of the operating and emergency modes of rectifiers as electronic converters of the industrial, renewable energy systems, etc.

articleTitle: Engineering Methods for Calculating the Process of Filtration of Vegetable Oils under Ultrasonic Cavitation Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The process of filtration of vegetable oils under conditions of ultrasonic cavitation is considered. The efficiency of use has been analyzed, and the prospects of using ultrasonic cavitation have been presented. The algorithm for processing the data obtained from experimental research during filtration under ultrasonic cavitation conditions is presented. Positive expectations have been confirmed by the results of theoretical research.

articleTitle: Analysis model for CO2 emissions of Romanian Power Plants fueled with Natural Gas
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Natural gas still plays an important role in energy generation in Romania. The paper analyzes, starting from statistical data related to the operational year 2022, through successive averaging, the effective daily power of electricity production from natural gas.All natural gas-fired thermoelectric plants were considered: steam turbines (ST), gas turbines (GT), gas-steam combined cycles (CCGT) and internal combustion engines (ICE), as well as the share of natural gas as fuel support in coal-based electricity production. It was thus possible to estimate the annual consumption of natural gas, from which the average annual carbon dioxide emission resulted. This result was compared with the declared values.

articleTitle: Investigation of measurement with cutting tool method for achieving accuracy with trial transition
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The application of cutting tool measurement method of parts surfaces during turning is under consideration. This method is applied for providing accuracy with trial transition in specific technological transitions and is particularly effective with the dominant influence of force deformations. This paper specifies the factors influencing measurements with the tool and investigates the errors that defines its accuracy. The pattern of measurement for achieving high accuracy is specified.

articleTitle: Concept for an IoT-based Electronic System for Smart Home Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This article presents a conceptual model of an electronic household automation, that should provide an affordable, multifunctional and reliable solution for home management. It is developed based on a microcomputer that collects and analyzes data for and from the system, communicating with one or more IoT devices. The conceptual model includes an architecture of the system, an operation algorithm describing its logic and an activity diagram, presenting the communication sequence. The proposed home automation system is implemented as an autonomous solution that doesn’t need Internet connectivity; however, such could be provided depending of the user’s preferences. The concept is developed to simplify the work of smart devices used in the household and enable them to optimize energy expenses while ensuring the security and comfort of their owners.

articleTitle: How To Educate Students in Technology Entrepreneuship
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The idea that innovation and entrepreneurship are key drivers in today’s engineering world, and the push for sustainable development, elaboration and development of Innovative Educational Program fostering competitiveness and flexibility of professionals in labor market by means of innovative, multidisciplinary, technology-based entrepreneurial education focusing on green deal and industries is crucial. A significant challenge for higher education institutions is preparing a new generation of engineer-entrepreneurs capable of blending technological and business cultures. They must be highly skilled in initiating and managing innovative, technology-based enterprises across various sectors, nationally and internationally. All of this underscores the importance of educating future entrepreneurs, particularly in the technological sector. The relevance of “Technological Entrepreneurship” education stems from the growing global demand for specialists with innovative thinking and entrepreneurial skills to meet modern business needs. The challenges in educating students in such programs are outlined in the paper.

articleTitle: Natural Disaster Frequency Model Program with Chebyshev Polynomial
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The frequency of extreme meteorological conditions such as floods, extreme temperatures, storms, fires and earthquakes in Bulgaria has been increasing in recent years. The consequences from them are affecting not only the population, but all domains of public life in the country. This implies a policy of adaption to climate changes for the purposes of decision-making process and mitigation of vulnerability of society towards risk factors and threats. The purpose of the report is to introduce a computer program operating in Matlab environment, which ensures the usage of model of natural disasters frequency Algorithm expressed by a Chelebyshev polynomial.

articleTitle: The role of human capital in the innovative development of the region
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The relevance of the study is determined by the presence of various approaches that define the role of value-added tax (VAT) in macroeconomic regulation. The aim of the research is to analyze scientific views on the impact of VAT on macroeconomic parameters of the Russian economy, as well as to substantiate macroeconomic factors influencing VAT receipts into the consolidated budget. The research methodology is based on principles recognizing taxation as an effective tool for macroeconomic regulation. The study employs general scientific methods, as well as correlation and regression analysis. The results of the scientific research presented in the article allow establishing a close relationship between VAT receipts into the consolidated budget and expenditures on final consumption, household income, inflation, gross domestic product, import and export volumes, as well as investment in fixed capital. The obtained results can be used to justify proposals for improving the calculation and payment procedures of VAT in order to ensure sustainable growth of the Russian economy

articleTitle: Study of the Noise Level in an Ice Cream Factory Working Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The noise exposure of workers in industrial halls is mainly due to noisy equipment whose acoustic characteristics are known. The category of workers who are near the equipment are the most exposed to noise. High noise levels can have negative effects on people. Sounds below or at the hearing threshold can cause stress to subjects in different environments who cannot receive the message of communication. At the same time, sounds with a high level of intensity can cause long-term damage to the human body depending on the time and intensity of the noise it has been subjected to, both indoors and in landscaped open spaces. The paper analyzes the level of noise generated by the operation of the equipment at the company that produces ice cream. The unit is in the city of Bacau and has a production area with several types of equipment. Measurements were made of the noise level generated by the production equipment in the company’s two halls, the production hall and the packaging hall. According to the results obtained, it can be concluded that the noise level values recorded in the evaluated working environment do not exceed the maximum allowed values.

articleTitle: Approach for Indirect Measurement of Chlorophyll and Phenophases of Maize Plant Using Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: An approach for Indirect Measurement of Chlorophyll and Phenophases of Maize Plant Using Image Processing is proposed in the paper. The proposed approach for indirect measurement of chlorophyll of maize plants and two main phases of plants: sweep and the presence of 11 leaves could be applied to a whole field or a part of it. Four color spaces are used in the research - RGB, HSV, Lab and XYZ. By applying the plant separation indices, it is possible to remove from the image pixels, that are not the object of the study. This allows only maize plants to be analyzed. Three informative color characteristics were found to distinguish the two classes of maize plants - a(Lab), b(Lab) and H(HSV). The color features are the first three informative features using the ReliefF algorithm. The accuracy for class 1 (sweeping phase) is $86,7 \%$ and for class 2 (phase 11 leaves) – 93,3%. Using ground measurements of the cholorphyll in plants for class 1 (sweeping phase) the values are 1,975 – 2,761 and for class 2 (phase 11 leaves): 1,449 – 1,842. Experimental verification of the accuracy of the proposed approach will be evaluated by increasing the number of field measurements and photographs.

articleTitle: Sensor-Driven Motorized Solution for Beehive Entrance Control
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This research introduces a new approach for the development of a stepper motor-operated door circuitry designed for controlling the access in a beehive. This solution allows users to manually or automatically adjust the position of the entrance door based on a decision-making algorithm using specialized sensors (ultrasonic, sound intensity, and temperature). Additionally, an atmospheric pressure sensor is used to conditionate the functioning. This integrated approach enables precise environmental monitoring, empowering beekeepers to take informed decisions for optimizing hive conditions. This solution aims to optimize beekeeping practices by providing a customizable and sensor-driven approach to hive entrance regulation, ultimately promoting efficient hive maintenance and colony well-being.

articleTitle: Severity Classification of Philippine Downy Mildew in Corn using Infrared Thermography and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Philippine Downy Mildew is one of the most damaging diseases affecting maize (corn) globally, causing significant damage to crops, lower yields, and increased production costs. This study proposes a plant disease detection and severity classification system that uses infrared thermography and deep learning. A novel dataset of 2279 corn thermograms was collected in the Institute of Plant Breeding field environment in Los Baños, Laguna, Philippines. Philippine Downy Mildew is categorized based on infection severity: Highly Resistant (0%-5%), Moderately Resistant (10%-20%), Moderately Susceptible (30%-50%), and Susceptible (60%- 100%). 3 CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) architectural models were compared for their performance with thermogram input. The models developed through customizing CNN architectures using ensemble learning include Model A (two-stage binary classification with NASNetMobile and MobileNetV2), Model B (multi-classification with EfficientNetB1 and NASNetMobile), and Model C (integrated Model B with binary classification using MobileNetV2). During the training of the customized CNN models, the use of transfer learning aided the increase in multiclassification accuracy. NASNetMobile obtained an accuracy of 93.8% for binary and 90.7% for multiclass, a two-class binary classification of MobileNetV2 obtained 95.8% and 96.9% respectively, and a multiclass EfficientNetB1 obtained 91.1%. During the actual field testing, models A, B, and C achieved an accuracy of 56.92%, 63.08%, and 76.92% respectively. This study demonstrates the potential of implementing infrared thermography with deep learning algorithms in agriculture for non-invasive plant disease severity rating.

articleTitle: Operational reliability of connection schemes of photovoltaic systems with three single-phase grid inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The paper points out the main advantages of the grid inverters, used to connect photovoltaic modules to the electrical grids. A methodology is presented for evaluating the operational reliability of schemes for connecting photovoltaic systems with single-phase grid inverters and one backup inverter provided. Results from the performed calculations are presented. Conclusions, useful both for the design stage and the operation of photovoltaic systems, are made.

articleTitle: Multisensor System for Measuring Air Components in Intelligent Animal Husbandry
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Modern animal husbandry prioritizes efficiency, but its consequences include animal welfare concerns, environmental pollution, and health impacts. Sensors play a crucial role in intelligent animal husbandry; they collect data from various aspects of the livestock and can detect various pollutants in the air. Most research in the field relies on standard sensor devices collecting data for individual parameters. Designing an affordable, easy-to-install multisensor device allows farmers to better monitor animal health and make better-informed decisions to manage their farms. In this paper a multisensor system for air quality measuring is proposed. The developed system is low cost, and it is based on open-source software. The data collected by the system will help to monitor and improve the environment in which the animals are kept.

articleTitle: Possibilities for using Magic Formula for characteristics prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: A study on the possibility to use known Magic formula for performance prediction in different technical areas is presented in this paper. How the Magic formula factors influence on the obtained curve is illustrated graphically. The results show the very wide possibility for application of Magic formula in modeling and prediction.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Apple Varieties Grown in Bulgaria
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The present study aims to investigate the possibilities of fluorescence and NIR spectroscopy for recognizing apple varieties grown in Bulgaria and to look for a correlation between optical parameters such as apple juice’s refractive index and the fruit’s color parameters. The focus is on the correlation between fluorescence spectra and apple variety using color, sugar content, and refractive index data, and the study of specific fluorophore in apple juice and their quantification using chemometrics techniques will be the subject of future scientific developments.We analyzed twenty samples of the studied varieties according to twelve optical indicators. Through cluster analysis, we divided the studied apples based on their similarity and distance according to the studied parameters.

articleTitle: Efficiency Evaluation and Performance Analysis of a Photovoltaic Park Connected to a 20 kV Distribution Network in Galati County, Romania
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: In this study, we delve into the design, installation, and performance evaluation of a photovoltaic park in Romania, connected to a 20 kV distribution network. With a peak capacity of 2640 kWp, the park capitalizes on Romania’s favorable climatic conditions and supportive renewable energy legislation. This comprehensive analysis encompasses both the photovoltaic panel sector and the power evacuation system. Specifically, the park’s transformer station has been designed with equipment that complies with European standards, utilizing cutting-edge technology common in recent energy distribution markets. The evaluation cover’s the park’s capacity to monitor operational efficiency and includes calculations of the performance ratio as well as various power losses due to temperature, dirt accumulation, inverter efficiencies, network challenges, and availability issues. Annually, the park contributes 3405 MWh of electricity to the grid, showcasing the effectiveness of photovoltaic installations in advancing sustainable energy solutions within regional power networks.

articleTitle: SWOT analysis in building a blockchain data sharing system
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The article analyzes the four main types of blockchains. These are open (public), closed (private), hybrid, and consortium. The latter two simultaneously and to varying degrees have characteristics of both open and closed. Their advantages and disadvantages are defined. However, the variety of platforms that cannot be accurately classified as a specific type of network makes it difficult for users to choose the appropriate one when sharing a given data stream. Therefore, a SWOT analysis of the two main types of chains - closed and open - was made to determine their advantages, disadvantages, threats, and opportunities. It was found that the main difficulty in choosing a type of blockchain is the constantly changing legislative framework. Furthermore, an appropriate platform can be selected according to the specifics of the material flow, privacy, security, quantity, speed, and others of data transmission.

articleTitle: Tailored Review on the Research in the Electric-Energy Efficiency of Transport Processes (Part 1): Bulk Materials and Fluids
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The adequate evaluation of the energy efficiency is an existing problem that needs to be solved. In this article, a new comparative study is presented covering published developments in a defined area of transportation processes provided with electrical energy. The methodology of this research consists of three stages: review of the existing developments; analysis on the used energy efficiency indicators; formulation of recommendations for improving these indicators. A widely accepted and universal indicator for evaluating energy efficiency has been identified, namely the total electrical energy consumed. A relatively common indicator is the efficiency coefficient indicator. It is characterized by the advantage of separating the useful and non-useful part of the energy, but the research done shows that it is limited, mainly for micro-climatic pump systems and oil wells, and less often for water supply systems. The application of this indicator should be expanded by developing generalized determination methods for a wide range of transportation processes provided with electrical energy.

articleTitle: CFD investigation of the intensity of heat transfer at forced convection of preheated air in a steel pipe
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This paper presents a CFD investigation in ABAQUS of the heat exchange intensity in curvilinear and linear zones of a steel pipe through which preheated air is flowing. The process intensity has been compared based on the average cross-section temperature differences. The research has been implemented as a continuation of a simulation study of the heat convection process in the pipe, as a result of which the temperature distribution of the fluid has been obtained, and the internal coefficient of convection heat exchange has been calculated. The external coefficient of convection heat exchange and the coefficient of overall heat exchange have been determined by ignoring the thermal resistance of the pipe wall. Heat exchange processes realized at three fluid velocities have been investigated. The impact of the fluid velocity on the intensity of the heat transfer process in the initial curvilinear zone of the pipe, on the values of the outer coefficient of heat convection and on the overall heat exchange coefficient, have been investigated. It has been found that the total decrease in velocity of $18.98 \%$ resulting in a decrease in the ratio of temperature differences in the two zones by $8.21 \%$. In the first range of speed change, $6.16 \%$ decrease in velocity leads to 6.04 $\%$ raise in the external heat convection coefficient and $2.30 \%$ raise in the coefficient of overall heat exchange. In the second velocity range, $13.66 \%$ decrease in velocity results in $16.72 \%$ decrease in the external heat convection coefficient and 14.79 $\%$ decrease in the overall heat transfer coefficient.

articleTitle: Methodology for the Selection of Raw Materials and Production of Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Based on the European requirements and the Paris Agreement to reduce the carbon footprint, the pros and cons of the main methods of extraction or production of hydrogen are analyzed. The comparison is based on the characteristics of the energy parameters of the energy sources and types of electrolyzers. The types of hydrogen are analyzed and a classification according to the amount of carbon emissions is proposed. Due to the heterogeneity of factors, choosing a method for obtaining hydrogen is a difficult task. Therefore, a methodology is proposed for choosing a solution according to defined factors such as efficiency, regulatory base, cost, carbon footprint, equipment, raw material sources, repairability, and level of innovation.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Experimental Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The world faces many challenges today and the distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems for local high-efficiency generation of electricity from sunlight seem to be one of the good solutions, but most of the population live in crowded urban environments, which creates a number of limiting factors. This study focuses on the design and implementation of an experimental photovoltaic installation in Ruse, Bulgaria, which allows the investigation of the impact of these factors on the efficiency of urban PV plants for optimization and education purposes. Initially, the goals towards the research facility are defined and the design and implementation of the installation is presented, including the orientation and positioning of the PV park, its schematic, and the key characteristics of the equipment used. Next, the first full year of operation of the research facility is analyzed by examining its energy generation profile. The winter months have about 6 times lower energy yields than the best summer ones and about 4-5 times lower on average compared to those for the other 3 seasons. This is due to the nearby buildings and trees, which create different shadows over the different seasons. The daily energy generation period during the winter is more than twice as short in comparison to that for the other seasons, while the peak daily winter energy yield is about $30 \%$ lower. The yearly energy yield per 1 kW peak installed PV panels is $1131.75 \mathrm{kWh} / \mathrm{kW}$, while the Global Solar Atlas suggests that the specific photovoltaic power output for Ruse is $1360.2 \mathrm{kWh} / \mathrm{kWp}$. The obtained exploitation results indicate that the experimental installation fully complies with the stated goals and allows investigating a number of urban scenarios.

articleTitle: Utilizing Computational Modeling for Real-Time Analysis of Energy Dynamics in Educational Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Nowadays, escalating energy costs and the enforcement of European energy directives, which extend to Romania, the urgent need to curb energy usage has gained considerable prominence, particularly concerning older buildings. To tackle this issue, we conducted dynamic simulations utilizing DesignBuilder software. Utilizing a Testo 885-2 thermal imager, we identified structural leaks and heat dissipation within buildings, complemented by the use of a Testo 435 device to gauge thermal transmittance of walls and roofs. These metrics served as vital inputs for the DesignBuilder simulations. Our study aimed to reduce energy consumption by enhancing the envelope components of buildings to meet the Nearly Zero Energy Building (nZEB) criteria stipulated by Romanian legislation for retrofitting educational structures. We observed a significant $71 \%$ decrease in thermal energy consumption, a $46 \%$ reduction in specific primary energy consumption and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions reduced by $55 \%$, when transitioning from the initial scenario to the most intricate setup. Regarding economic viability, the most elaborate scenario demonstrated a 12-year payback period, even in the absence of external funding from governmental initiatives. This investigation underscores the considerable potential for energy conservation and economic advantages achievable through the adoption of energy-efficient building solutions.

articleTitle: Communication Challenges in Smart Irrigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Developing smart irrigation systems based on technologies such as the Internet of Things, sensors, field communication technologies, WSNs and automated systems enables farmers to manage soil irrigation through improved irrigation control and planning techniques. At the same time, the implementation and operation of these systems, having different scales, face different challenges that could improve the proper management and efficiency of the systems. A serious part of these challenges related to constructing and operating the communication networks in IIS. This work analyses the most appropriate communication protocols in the different layers of IIS. Their applicability in IIS from an agricultural farm scale perspective is discussed. Six other groups of communication challenges have been identified and analysed, including technical limitations, Environmental factors, Data management, Human intervention, Integration challenges, and Cyber security. Recommendations are given for their solution to help IIS designers and users.

articleTitle: Enhancing Quality Management Systems with Knowledge Management in a University Context
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: In recent years, the gap between perceptions and knowledge transfer widens significantly. This trend is especially pronounced as Generation Z representatives are becoming more influential at the organizational level. The undisputedly most popular management systems standards are based on the ISO 9000 series for quality management systems. The turn of the century has witnessed the integration of these systems with environmental, occupational health and safety, information security, and other management systems depending on the context and focus of the organization. Even more impactful changes are due to be published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in 2024 as amendments to international standards for management systems. Expectedly, they are mainly related to climate action changes. At present, the integration of management systems at the University of Ruse, Bulgaria, involves such aspects as innovation management, business continuity, and knowledge management systems. The paper extends previously published research dealing with curriculum design and an new pedagogical approach to teaching and learning for the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), coupled with integrated management systems. This paper highlights best practices, methodologies, and tools for knowledge management that can enhance the effect that management systems can exert on the performance of educational organizations in general, and more specifically - at the University of Ruse, Bulgaria.

articleTitle: The Role of Environmental Non-Governmental Organizations in Achieving Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: This report analyses and highlights the main benefits of the activities of environmental non-governmental organisations in the direction of achieving energy efficiency. A case study of a specific ecological non-governmental organisation - a leader in the integration of innovations and solutions for energy efficiency, and with many years of experience and participation in the development of international policies in the field of sustainable consumption of resources - has been examined. Based on the specific activities and functions of the research object, the significant role of the non-profit legal entity sector in the energy transition process and global environmental protection policies has been identified. Part of their role includes collecting, analysing, and disseminating information, providing data and services, and assessing and monitoring environmental agreements. The main conclusions can serve to multiply the effects or avoid the risks on the part of regional and national non-profit organisations in their participation in the development of local policies in the field of energy independence and environmental protection.

articleTitle: Increase in Convective Intensity Drying of Sweet Root Fruits
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Drying crops is a necessary condition for better storage of the crop and the nutrients contained in it. At the same time, the drying process is energy-intensive and up to $25 \%$ of energy is spent on it. This work is devoted to starch-containing raw materials, in particular, sweet potato roots. The goal is to study the convective dehydration of root crops and find ways to intensify the process, reducing drying time, heat consumption and ensuring maximum preservation of the natural properties of raw materials. The object of the study is the root crops of orange sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas L.). On the basis of the conducted research, rational conditions for thermo-moisture processing of sweet potato roots were determined, in particular, the modes of preliminary processing of sweet potato roots were defined and new staged drying modes were developed, which significantly reduces the duration of drying. The paper examines the moisture exchange during dehydration of sweet potato root crops, summarizes the research results, calculates the total duration of the root crop drying process, and provides the formula for the duration of the process. The result of the work is a reduction in the duration of drying, a reduction in heat consumption by $15 \%$, and obtaining high-quality dried products that are close to the natural properties of the material.

articleTitle: Study of Bulgarian Consumers’ Attitude Towards the Use of Sunflower Husk Pellets
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: The following study provides information about the quality of sunflower husk pellets produced by Bulgarian manufacturers, helping consumers in selecting the most suitable pellets for their needs and heating installations. A consumer opinion research was conducted for examining customers’ attitude towards the use of such pellets. It aids in shaping manufacturers’ marketing strategies and product improvement. In order to establish the quality and reliability of sunflower pellets, experimental measurements were made of some of the energy characteristics of the most common brands of sunflower husks in the Bulgarian market. The results of these experimental measurements were compared with the information provided on the packaging of the sunflower pellets by the respective manufacturers. The analysis of the results shows that all of the studied parameters meet the conditions for quality certification. This is essential for all consumers as it certifies that the product meets certain quality and performance standards. Conducting such research is essential to ensure consistency of pellet quality and facilitate consumers’ selection and purchasing process when using sunflower husks as an alternative raw material.

articleTitle: Sociological imagination on green technology: the influence of occupational and professional background on the architectural photovoltaic application
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Clients with different occupational backgrounds may perceive green technology and systems differently. This study examines the impact of individuals’ occupational and professional backgrounds on their ability to perceive the benefits and advantages of sustainable technologies such as solar photovoltaic (PV). In addition, it investigates the impact of occupational and professional background on the willingness to install and integrate PV technology in residential units in the future. The study focuses on professionals in the building industry, including those in the energy, construction, design, and architecture sectors and experts from other industries. A survey was conducted to gather participants’ knowledge, concerns, familiarity, and acceptance of PV systems. Descriptive statistics, regression analysis, correlation analysis, and one-way ANOVA were used to analyze the data. The findings show that occupational and professional backgrounds influence individuals’ choices since they possess a foundation in their education and work experiences. Workers in the building industry recorded higher positive percentages toward PV technology. The level of knowledge is the most significant factor in the perception and desire for PV among professionals in the building industry. The impact of the concern, familiarity, and satisfaction levels was statistically negligible. Professionals’ knowledge and expertise substantially affect the energy and construction sectors. The analysis of the findings demonstrates variations among individuals according to their occupational backgrounds. The research has confirmed that professional background significantly influences how technology is perceived and embraced. This study provides insights into the impact of awareness on accepting and using green technologies.

articleTitle: Software uses in precision agriculture based on drone image processing – A review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Precision agriculture defined as a holistic and environmentally friendly method consists of the application of technologies, principles and strategies for the intelligent management of agricultural production in relation to the reality of real needs and spatial and temporal variability. Data processing software are essential tools in the implementation and development of agriculture. The link between the two is based on the advanced processing capacity of data captured by drones, which is essential in the analysis and optimization of agricultural crops. Integrating precision agriculture with specialized software enables farmers to obtain detailed information to identify the best ways to maximize farm yields and sustainability. This combination of advanced technologies brings significant benefits to the efficiency, productivity and profitability of modern farming. This paper identifies the advantages of using photogrammetry software capable of making reflectance measurements that improve precision and accuracy in comparative evaluations of phenotyping data for cereal propagating material. Orthophoto maps created using digital photogrammetry techniques use a digital terrain model of the earth’s surface and a digital aerial image geometry correction that eliminates geometric distortions caused by field conditions and data collection instruments.

articleTitle: Vegetable biomass – source of green hydrogen production through gasification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Energy Efficiency and Agricultural Engineering (EE&AE)
abstract: Through the gasification of vegetable (agricultural) biomass, as well as forest biomass, a combustible gas with a significant content of green hydrogen is obtained. This fuel will have to be integrated into a neutral society from the point of view of hydrogen emission, over the concept issued in Kyoto in 1996. In the paper, in the first part, solutions for an ecological transition society are analyzed. The progress achieved in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas capture allows, for the transition period, the parallel use of renewable energy sources with those that use fossil or synthetic fuels. The achievements in the field of biomass gasification are discussed in the second part of the paper. The gasification of vegetable biomass is in an early phase, of research and achievements at the stage of pilot plants. The work contains results of the gasification of vegetable biomass, on a 4 kW pilot plant, with references to the quality of the fuel gas obtained, both by the hydrogen content and by the calorific power. The paper also contains an image regarding the combustion of gasogen gas, during the gasification of vegetable biomass represented by walnut shells.
